title: Two Identical Choices
title_ja: 同じ内容の二つの選択肢
fact_notes: 人物、具体的な出来事・実験・記録は架空の教材例。実在の調査や統計の結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A teacher gave two groups of students different descriptions of the same imaginary school trip.
sentences.ja: 先生は二つの生徒グループに同じ架空の校外学習について異なる説明を渡した。

sentences.en: The first description emphasized that most of the activities would take place outdoors.
sentences.ja: 最初の説明は活動の大半が屋外で行われることを強調した。

sentences.en: The second emphasized that a small number of activities would take place indoors.
sentences.ja: 二つ目は少数の活動が屋内で行われることを強調した。

sentences.en: Both descriptions included the same complete schedule and exactly the same information about the trip.
sentences.ja: どちらにも同じ完全な日程とまったく同じ情報が含まれていた。

sentences.en: The teacher asked students to write down their initial impressions before discussing the two descriptions.
sentences.ja: 先生は二つの説明を議論する前に最初の印象を書き留めるよう求めた。

sentences.en: Some students mentioned the outdoor experience, while others focused on the indoor activities.
sentences.ja: 屋外体験に触れる生徒もいれば、屋内活動に注目する生徒もいた。

sentences.en: After comparing the two descriptions, they discovered that the actual schedules were identical.
sentences.ja: 二つの説明を比較した後、実際の日程が同一だと分かった。

sentences.en: They became curious about why different words could direct attention toward different parts of the same information.
sentences.ja: 異なる言葉が同じ情報の別の部分に注意を向けさせる理由に興味を持った。

sentences.en: The teacher then invited the students to design two announcements for an imaginary school festival.
sentences.ja: 次に先生は架空の学校祭の告知文を二種類作るよう生徒に求めた。

sentences.en: One announcement emphasized the number of activities that visitors could enjoy without paying.
sentences.ja: 一方は来場者が無料で楽しめる活動の数を強調した。

sentences.en: The other emphasized the activities for which visitors would need to buy a ticket.
sentences.ja: もう一方はチケットを買う必要のある活動を強調した。

sentences.en: The students checked that neither announcement contained false facts or omitted the complete price list.
sentences.ja: どちらにも虚偽の事実がなく完全な価格一覧が省略されていないことを確認した。

sentences.en: During their discussion, the class considered whether choosing an emphasis could ever be misleading.
sentences.ja: 議論でクラスは強調する点を選ぶことが誤解を招く場合があるか考えた。

sentences.en: They agreed that a short announcement could not give equal attention to every detail.
sentences.ja: 短い告知ですべての詳細に等しく注意を向けることはできないと合意した。

sentences.en: However, the writer should not hide important information that might change a reader's decision.
sentences.ja: しかし書き手は読み手の判断を変え得る重要な情報を隠すべきではない。

sentences.en: The students suggested adding a clear summary so readers could examine the relevant facts for themselves.
sentences.ja: 読み手が関連する事実を自分で調べられるよう明確な要約を加えることを提案した。

sentences.en: The activity showed the students that language can influence which details people notice first.
sentences.ja: 活動から、言葉は人が最初にどの詳細に気づくかに影響し得ると学んだ。

sentences.en: This did not mean that everyone would react to the same description in the same way.
sentences.ja: これは全員が同じ説明に同じように反応するという意味ではなかった。

sentences.en: Instead, the students learned to pause and compare the information before forming a final judgment.
sentences.ja: むしろ最終判断を下す前に一度立ち止まり、情報を比較することを学んだ。

sentences.en: They concluded that careful reading begins by asking what the writer has chosen to emphasize.
sentences.ja: 慎重な読解は書き手が何を強調することにしたか尋ねることから始まると結論づけた。

vocabulary.definition: statements showing what something is like
existing in imagination rather than reality
a plan of events and times
something a person takes part in
cause something to move toward a target
likely to cause a wrong impression
having the same amount or status
a conclusion about what to do
a short account of main facts
look at or think about carefully

questions.prompt: What differed between the trip descriptions?
questions.explanation_ja: 強調点が異なるだけだった。
完全な日程は同一だった。

questions.prompt: When did students write their first impressions?
options: When they returned from a holiday.
questions.explanation_ja: 二つを議論する前に書いた。

questions.prompt: Why were some students interested in the different wording?
options: It proved every student had the same impression.
It appeared to direct attention to different details.
It prevented students from reading the description.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ情報でも注目点が異なった。

questions.prompt: What did one festival announcement emphasize?
options: Activities visitors could enjoy for free.
The location of a real school trip.
questions.explanation_ja: 無料で楽しめる活動を強調。

questions.prompt: What did the students check about both announcements?
options: Both promised all activities were free.
Both used exactly the same opening sentence.
Neither omitted the complete price list.
questions.explanation_ja: 料金一覧を省略しないよう確認した。

options: Likely to create a wrong impression.
questions.explanation_ja: 誤った印象を与え得るという意味。

questions.prompt: When can selecting an emphasis become problematic?
options: When important information affecting a decision is hidden.
When every price is clearly listed.
Whenever readers can check the details.
questions.explanation_ja: 判断に影響する情報を隠すことが問題。

questions.prompt: What did the students learn to do before a final judgment?
options: Accept the first impression without question.
questions.explanation_ja: 立ち止まり情報を比較する。

options: Identical facts always produce identical reactions.
Pay attention to how wording directs attention before judging information.
Teachers should avoid giving any announcements.
questions.explanation_ja: 言葉の強調点を確認して判断すること。

grammar.explanation_ja: wouldは過去から見た未来を表す。

grammar.focus: that the actual schedules were identical
for which visitors would need to buy a ticket
grammar.explanation_ja: 前置詞＋関係代名詞whichがactivitiesを修飾する。

grammar.focus: did not mean that everyone would react
grammar.explanation_ja: that節はmeanの内容、否定は全員同様という意味ではないことを示す。

discourse.role_ja: 二つの注目点を対比する。
活動の次の段階を示す。
すべての詳細を示せないことと重要な情報を隠さない責任を対比。
極端な一般化を避け、学んだ対応を示す。

paraphrases.source: The first description emphasized that most of the activities would take place outdoors.
paraphrases.rewrite: The first version drew attention to the fact that most events were planned for outside.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 最初の説明は屋外の活動を強調。

paraphrases.source: After comparing the two descriptions, they discovered that the actual schedules were identical.
paraphrases.rewrite: Once they compared the two texts, they found that both described exactly the same timetable.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 比較すると日程が同じと分かった。

paraphrases.source: The other emphasized the activities for which visitors would need to buy a ticket.
paraphrases.rewrite: The other version highlighted the activities that required a paid ticket.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 有料の活動を強調した。

paraphrases.source: This did not mean that everyone would react to the same description in the same way.
paraphrases.rewrite: The activity did not imply that every person would respond identically to a particular description.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 反応が全員同じとは限らない。

cloze.explanation_ja: 完全に同じ情報だった。
価格一覧を省略していないと確認。
情報を比較して最終判断。
